one_liner: A male patient with metopic synostosis and trigonocephaly underwent successful bilateral orbital frontal zygomatic craniotomy and reconstruction without complications.

procedures.name: Bilateral orbital frontal zygomatic craniotomy (skull base approach)
procedures.outcome: Successful reconstruction with about 1 cm advancement and no complications

procedures.name: Bilateral orbital advancement with bone grafts
Bilateral forehead reconstruction with autologous graft
Advancement of the temporalis muscle bilaterally
Barrel-stave osteotomies of the parietal bones

course.narrative: The patient underwent general anesthesia and was positioned supine. A bicoronal zigzag incision was made, followed by craniectomy outlining and bur hole drilling. Bilateral craniotomies were performed using a Midas Rex drill, and the midline piece was elevated. Orbital osteotomies and bone scoring were executed to enable orbital advancement. Bone grafts were secured with a shelf created on the superior orbital rim. Temporalis muscle advancement and barrel-stave osteotomies of the parietal bones were performed to normalize bone contour. Blood loss was approximately 300 to 400 mL, which was replaced with packed cells and fresh frozen plasma. The reconstruction achieved about 1 cm advancement with good cosmetic results. The wound was closed in layers. The patient tolerated the procedure well with no complications.
